supported_routes.question: describe one numeric outcome
supported_routes.method: distribution, centre, spread and an honest graph
supported_routes.claim_limit: sample description does not automatically describe a population

supported_routes.question: associate two numeric variables
supported_routes.method: scatterplot and correlation, followed by linear regression when the question needs a conditional mean

supported_routes.question: compare a numeric outcome across two independent groups
supported_routes.design: different independent units in the two groups
supported_routes.claim_limit: group membership alone supplies no causal meaning

supported_routes.question: compare a numeric outcome across exactly two linked measurements
supported_routes.design: the same unit measured exactly twice or a pair fixed by design
supported_routes.method: paired t test on within-pair differences
supported_routes.claim_limit: pairing must be preserved from the design and does not establish causation

supported_routes.question: compare a numeric outcome across more than two independent groups
supported_routes.design: one independent group membership per unit
supported_routes.method: ANOVA as a linear model with planned or multiplicity-protected comparisons
supported_routes.claim_limit: the omnibus test does not identify which groups differ

supported_routes.question: associate two categorical variables
supported_routes.method: contingency table and chi-square, or Fisher exact test for a small table with a thin approximation
supported_routes.claim_limit: no mechanical expected-frequency threshold replaces examination of the table

supported_routes.question: estimate a population mean or proportion
supported_routes.design: a sampling design that supports the target population
supported_routes.method: point estimate and interval appropriate to the sampling design
supported_routes.claim_limit: sampling uncertainty does not cover selection, coverage or measurement bias

supported_routes.question: model a numeric outcome with multiple predictors
read a published binary-outcome result
supported_routes.design: published model output with a named reference group
supported_routes.method: read the outcome, reference group, odds ratio and interval without refitting
supported_routes.claim_limit: the book does not fit or diagnose a logistic model

stop_routes.reason: the independence unit or link between rows is not resolved
stop_routes.referral: record the unit, linkage and estimand, then consult a methods specialist or a source for that exact design

stop_routes.reason: the book supports exactly two linked quantitative measurements but no broader repeated-data model
stop_routes.referral: seek a method that preserves every repetition and its time structure

stop_routes.reason: rows within a group may share variation
stop_routes.referral: seek a method whose uncertainty preserves clustering and all design levels
seek a method that explicitly preserves temporal dependence

stop_routes.reason: ties between units violate an independent-row analysis
stop_routes.referral: seek a method that preserves nodes, ties and the observed network boundary

stop_routes.reason: the book recognises design effects and effective sample size but does not teach complex-survey variance
stop_routes.referral: seek a procedure and documentation that use the full sampling design

stop_routes.reason: the book teaches reading odds ratios but not logistic-model fitting or diagnostics
stop_routes.referral: use the reading bridge in Chapter 16, then seek an outside method for fitting

stop_routes.reason: adjustment alone does not identify a causal effect
stop_routes.referral: specify a defensible design and identification strategy before choosing an estimator

stop_routes.reason: the book teaches reading replication estimates and a forest plot but no meta-analysis computation
stop_routes.referral: seek an outside method for the synthesis estimand, assumptions and uncertainty
